Instruction account lookup and borrow helpers, plus signer queries.

# Purpose
This C file implements helper functions for `fd_exec_instr_ctx_t`, which is the instruction execution context used during transaction processing. The functions connect instruction-level account references to transaction-level account data. They search for accounts by public key, map instruction account indexes to transaction account indexes, and return account keys from the transaction context. The file also provides access to the last program account for an instruction.

The file also handles account borrowing for execution. Functions such as [`fd_exec_instr_ctx_try_borrow_account`](<#fd_exec_instr_ctx_try_borrow_account>), [`fd_exec_instr_ctx_try_borrow_instr_account`](<#fd_exec_instr_ctx_try_borrow_instr_account>), and [`fd_exec_instr_ctx_try_borrow_instr_account_with_key`](<#fd_exec_instr_ctx_try_borrow_instr_account_with_key>) locate an account, check that it can be borrowed, and create a `fd_borrowed_account_t` on success. Other helpers collect signer keys and test whether a given public key signed the instruction. The code uses transaction context APIs and returns execution error codes when an account is missing, cannot be borrowed, or does not match the expected instruction account list.
